role: Visual Target Director / independent scene-art reviewer
scope: Independent Workstream-13 scene/character art direction only; no runtime wiring or catalog-canonical authority

strengths: Substantially stronger volumetric furniture, textile and daylight response than the current flat/vector environment direction.
Bed-left / desk-right composition is compatible with the target hierarchy and leaves useful foreground floor area for a separate avatar.
No copied third-party characters, logos, UI, text or flattened screenshot content are baked into the scene.
reworkReasons: The brightest window is centered directly behind the intended avatar corridor, competing with the character silhouette; the original target keeps the avatar as the central visual focus rather than placing the strongest white hotspot behind her.
The room currently reads closer to a clean semi-realistic children’s bedroom than the denser stylized premium block-world / toy-game environment shown by the approved reference.
Prop and shelf density is too sparse for the target: the approved reference uses layered collectibles, décor, lighting and activity cues around the hero while still leaving the center playable.

The scene needs stronger game-specific shape language and saturated material accents so cobalt/navy chrome, the avatar and collectible panels feel like one authored world rather than UI floating over a generic room render.
measurableRepairContract: Keep an avatar-safe corridor approximately x=36–64% of the 1408px frame and y=18–88%; move or diffuse the dominant window hotspot so the brightest architectural opening is not centered behind that corridor.

Preserve bed-left and desk-right anchors, but add roughly 4–7 distinct secondary environmental props across the side zones (shelves/books/soft lights/plants/collectible objects) without adding UI text or logos.
Increase stylization through chunkier rounded furniture silhouettes, clearer bevels/edge highlights and more saturated blush/lilac/cyan/gold material accents; avoid photorealistic neutral surfaces.
Keep top-center and far-right overlay zones visually calm enough for HUD/Dream Goal chrome; detail can increase around them but should not introduce high-frequency text-like marks.
Retain the clean center floor and separate-character architecture; do not bake the avatar, buddy, navigation, counters or cards into the background.

handoff.13: Produce a v2 environment using the repair contract above; preserve the strong material depth and bed-left/desk-right structure while fixing the central hotspot, density and toy-game stylization.
handoff.14: Do not composition-approve v1 for runtime wiring; review v2 for overlay-safe zones, format/performance and real-browser composition after Workstream 13 stages it.
handoff.15: No runtime handoff is recommended for v1. Keep Workstream 09 active environment unchanged until a revised independently accepted candidate exists.

strengths: The exact staged pixels are polished and genuinely dimensional: hair, jacket, denim, headset and shoes have readable volume, soft material response and controlled cyan/warm rim lighting rather than flat vector treatment.
Long brown hair and cat-ear headset preserve the two strongest high-level identity markers from all three original reference screens.
The full and 896px companion retain a clean, child-appropriate silhouette with verified transparent surround, so the figure can be composited separately from scene backgrounds.
No baked UI, text, counters, logos or scene pixels are present; the candidate remains isolated key art rather than a fake running-game screenshot.
reworkReasons: The authoritative Home/Store/Quest avatar has a chunky block-world/toy-game silhouette with squared forearms and hands, broad rectangular legs and oversized blocky shoes. This candidate changes that core identity into a generic rounded chibi figure with articulated fingers, narrower limbs and conventional human proportions.

The face reads as a different character despite the matching hair/headset cues: the references use very high-contrast black oval eyes or a wink, pronounced cheek marks and a wide open joyful mouth, while this candidate uses brown irises, softer realistic eyelids and a small closed smile.

The headset silhouette is directionally correct, but its pale lavender earcups and soft pastel construction drift from the reference’s stronger hot-pink/black cat-headset identity, reducing instant cross-screen recognition.

Because the jacket, shirt, jeans and shoes are flattened into this one character layer, the image is safe only as noncanonical visual guidance/key art. It must never become a runtime avatar substitute that overrides the player’s equipped catalog state.
repairContract: Preserve the current transparent full-body architecture, clean cutout, long brown hair, premium material depth and controlled cyan/warm key lighting.

Move the base body silhouette materially closer to the originals: chunkier block-world proportions, squared/boxier forearms and hands, thicker rectangular legs and larger toy-like shoes while keeping the pose readable.

Restore the reference facial language: larger high-contrast near-black oval eyes, stronger cheek/blush marks and a wider open cheerful expression; keep enough facial simplicity to read consistently beside the Home, Store and Quest avatar at UI scale.

Push the cat-ear headset toward the reference identity with stronger hot-pink outer structure and darker earcup/accent contrast; preserve the cat-ear silhouette and avoid realistic consumer-brand detailing.

Keep all visible clothing/accessories explicitly noncanonical guidance. If this art is ever adapted for runtime use, wardrobe/accessories must be separate/swappable components driven by equipped state rather than baked into the avatar layer.

handoff.13: Produce a bounded v2 avatar key-art candidate that keeps v1's material/lighting quality but repairs face identity and block-world body proportions. Do not treat the visible outfit as canonical.
handoff.14: Composition/performance ownership remains with reviewer 14; this reviewer-01 verdict is art/identity only and makes no screenshot-parity claim.
handoff.15: Keep v1 out of runtime/canonical wiring. Route a new exact repo-stored hash back to reviewer 01 only after the bounded identity/proportion repair is staged with readback evidence.
